messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: p99 latency for /v1/generate streaming has breached 8s for the past 3m across dedicated-pool-42. Potential capacity saturation. Pager triggered to #incidents.
Ava (oncall): I'm awake, looking now. Any customer-reported errors?
Lina (support): No direct customer tickets yet, but a handful of 504s from a large customer (acme-inc) started ~7m ago. I've CC'd their AM.
Diego: Metrics I see: dedicated-pool-42 GPU utilization at 96-99%, queue depth jumped from ~30 -> 420 in last 2m, average warmup latency per model shard ~1.8s. Autoscaler hasn't added nodes in last 5m.
Priya: Confirming streaming stalls: CRT logs show repeated `stream_send_timeout` backoff for internal stream dispatch loops. p95 ~1.2s but p99 ~9.3s.
Samir: Autoscaler events: threshold was hit, triggered scale but the warmup hooks delayed ready state because warmup container init stalled on `kvcache` restore. `warmup_time` metric per host shows a tail at 45s.
Ava (oncall): So chain is: burst -> queue depth -> autoscaler triggered -> new hosts start but warmup slow -> requests pile -> tail latency. Correct?
Diego: Yep. Also saw a spike in model memory reclaim thrashing on some hosts which slowed warmup. Suspect a concurrent maintenance job triggered on that pool earlier.
Ken (eng-platform): I see a maintenance job rolling GPUs in pool-42 at ~2076541980 that shouldn't run during high traffic. Investigating why schedule overlapped.
Priya: Customer-impact estimate: ~12% of requests to dedicated-pool-42 experienced p99>8s, streaming sessions sometimes stalled and reconnected. No ERROR 5xx spike except client-side timeouts.
Lina (support): Notifying ACME support channel: "We're investigating increased latency and streaming stalls, possible temporary throttling on your dedicated pool. We'll provide ETA in 15m."
Samir: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Manual emergency scale up of pool-42 (add 4 nodes) 2) Route new traffic away from pool-42 to fallback pool (platform config) 3) Force enable quick-warmup path (skip kvcache restore) for new instances 4) Apply manual throttling on non-critical routes to relieve queue.
Ava (oncall): I can do manual scale-up. Any risks?
Ken (eng-platform): Manual scale risk: if warmup path is slow it'll just add more hosts that sit in warming state and increase overall load. Routing traffic out is cleaner if fallback compatible models exist.
Diego: Fallback pool (pool-11) has compatible model variants but is at 70% util, can absorb some burst. Routing will require updating routing policy to prefer pool-11 for tenant tags with `dedicated-pool-42` until healthy. Takes ~30s to flip.
Priya: Quick-warmup (skip kvcache) would reduce warmup from ~45s -> ~6s but causes first few requests on warm hosts to be 1-2x slower and increases token cost due to recompute.
Ava (oncall): Plan: 1) Route 50% of new traffic to pool-11 now. 2) Trigger quick-warmup on 3 new nodes in pool-42. 3) If queue depth doesn't fall in 3m, manual add +4 nodes. 4) Keep customers notified.
Samir: Ack. I'll open the routing flip: `PATCH /internal/routing/policy pool-preference` -> set weight pool-11=50 pool-42=50.
Ken (eng-platform): I'll stand by to cancel maintenance roll if it's still running. How to trigger quick-warmup?
Diego: Quick-warmup toggle: `POST /admin/pools/42/warmup?mode=fast&skip_kv=true` (requires ops role). Will add logs: `warmup_mode=fast started_by=Ava`.
Ava (oncall): Doing routing flip now. 
Ava (oncall): /me runs: `curl -X PATCH "https://controlplane.internal/routing/pool-weights" -d '{"pool-11":50,"pool-42":50}'`
incident-bot: Routing change applied by Ava (oncall) at 2076543290.
Diego: Routing change visible in metrics: incoming traffic to pool-11 now up 48%, pool-42 down ~46%. Queue depth dropping from 420 -> 190. Good signal.
Ava (oncall): Initiating quick-warmup on 3 nodes. `POST /admin/pools/42/warmup?mode=fast&count=3&skip_kv=true`
Samir: Quick-warmup logs show new hosts started, warmup_time ~5.8s for nodes 42-7..9. They hit ready state.
Priya: Observability: p99 reduced from 9.3s -> 5.2s in 90s after routing flip. Streaming stalls still happening intermittently but decreasing.
Lina (support): ACME update: "Latency reduced but some streaming stalls persisted. We've applied a temporary routing change on our side. Awaiting full mitigation"
Ken (eng-platform): Maintenance job was indeed active on pool-42; I killed the job and set hold for next 2h. It was an automated reclamation that mis-scheduled.
Ava (oncall): Queue depth now steady ~70, GPU util pool-42 ~82%, pool-11 ~78%. p99 trending toward SLO.
Diego: Note: autoscaler logs show missed scale windows due to `warmup_timeout_threshold` set to 40s. Need to reduce threshold to 15s or implement fast-warmup fallback. Filed short ticket: CL-4721.
Priya: Customer impact summary for postmortem: ~18 minutes of elevated p99 > SLO, ~7% of streaming sessions experienced stalls needing reconnects, primary cause: pool exhaustion compounded by autoscaler warmup latency and overlapping maintenance.
Samir: For immediate follow-ups: 1) adjust autoscaler warmup thresholds + fallback path 2) add scheduling guard to block maintenance during high load 3) add circuit-breaker routing to proactively shift traffic when queue depth > 200 for 1m.
Ken (eng-platform): Agree. I'll own the maintenance scheduling guard. Ava, can you add the circuit-breaker ticket?
Ava (oncall): I'll create the ticket and link CL-4721. Also scheduling guard ticket CL-4722.
Lina (support): I'll follow up with ACME and share timeline and remediation steps.
Priya: Will collect logs for the 3 impacted warmup hosts and attach to incident. Also will run a replay of request traces to validate no data loss.
Ava (oncall): Final status for now: mitigations applied, p99 dropping toward SLO, routing partially shifted, quick-warmup active, maintenance halted. Keeping thread open for verification 30m. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by Ava (oncall) at 2076543540. Incident severity: SEV2.
Diego: One more datapoint: we saw elevated kernel OOM kills on one host earlier, that's likely why kvcache restore slowed. I'll add to logs.
Samir: Triage notes: root cause = combinatorial: traffic burst + pool capacity near threshold + autoscaler warmup path and maintenance overlap -> delayed scale and queue amplification -> tail latency.
Ava (oncall): Thanks all. If anything regresses ping me directly. I'll file the postmortem skeleton after stabilization.
Lina (support): ACME acknowledged and will keep monitor.
Ken (eng-platform): I'll put a hard hold on maintenance and follow-up with infra team.
incident-bot: Thread will be auto-closed in 48h if no activity."
